Third-party AI agents are external personal assistants (not from your bank) that you authorize to access accounts, often via credentials or APIs. They can check balances, pay bills, transfer funds, or shop.

note_tweet.text:
The most useful question about AI agents is not “Which one is smartest?” It is “What work can it reliably complete, under whose control, and with what evidence?”

Consider five names in the current conversation: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Grok Bot, Meta Muse and ChatGPT Dots. A fair comparison cannot begin with a leaderboard. It needs the same task, the same access boundaries and the same definition of success.

For OpenClaw, examine how its self-hosting, persistent memory and skills fit a workflow you actually own. For Hermes Agent, test the specific task you would delegate and inspect the result. For Grok Bot, ask which source material and actions are available in your intended setup. For Meta Muse and ChatGPT Dots, distinguish announced features from capabilities that have been independently demonstrated. Where product details are unclear, mark them as unknown rather than filling the gap with assumptions.

Then run a small, repeatable trial. Give each candidate one bounded job: find a source, extract a fact, produce a draft, and show the source. Record accuracy, time to completion, required human corrections and whether the agent stayed within its permissions. Repeat the trial before making a purchasing or deployment decision.

This approach is less exciting than a viral demo. It is far more useful when an agent is expected to work inside a real business process. The winner is not the loudest product. It is the one that makes a measurable improvement without hiding the work or weakening your controls.

Hermes Agent Memory and Cost

MarkTechPost compared personal AI agents on memory security defaults and cost in November 2026.

Hermes Agent stores memory in Markdown files and searchable SQLite sessions.

Its unanswered approval prompts are denied after 300 seconds.

OpenClaw supports 26 channels and gives full host access by default.

An audit found 341 malicious entries among 2857 ClawHub skills.

Gemini Spark costs $19.99 per month on Google's AI Pro plan in the US.

OpenAI dots are included in eligible ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium plans.

Meta Muse offers a free tier plus $20 and $100 monthly plans.
